fields.aglebov\n\n 2013-08-11 07:54\n\ndevelope:
Well, shall I say that the concept of "surnames of patronymic origin" is puzzling for a Russian-speaking user in the first place? For instance, "Иванов" is exactly a surname of patronymic origin (i.e. a family name derived from an earlier patronymic name), but is not a patronymic name any more (not since the beginning of the 20th century). When I started using Gramps, I marked my own last name (Глебов) as being of patronymic origin, but then did not find the 'origin' field particularly useful, so stopped filling it. At the same time, I can imagine that somebody might use the 'origin' field for its intended purpose, that is marking the origin of family names, and would object to (or get surprised by) excluding some of them from the count of unique surnames.
Speculating on the best solution, I guess Gramps needs some sort of pluggable language/culture modules, that can be developed by people acquainted with the corresponding cultures independently, as one-solution-fits-all does not seem to be possible. I understand that this is not going to happen in 3.4.7, more likely in 5.0, 6.0, etc.
